Subject: Pricing envelope: 'flip' discount clause and packaging alignment

Emma / Tim —

Quick note from our side on the pricing envelope and one clause we've seen repeatedly cause confusion in previous deals: the "flip" discount mechanic that immediately reverts a committed discount when usage dips below a threshold in a billing month. Novus's usage profile (bursty with seasonal dips) makes that binary flip risky for both sides.

Two asks:
- Can you confirm whether Novus would accept a smoothing/grace approach (example below) instead of an instantaneous flip?
- We also need to clarify packaging: when we reference "Pack A" in the order form, does that include the token carryover you described on the call, or is it strictly per-month? That changes which tier you land in.

Suggested compromise (high level):
- Flip is permitted but transition uses a 60-day smoothing window (two billing periods). If usage falls below commit for one month, a warning is issued and no price change occurs; only after two consecutive months below threshold does the lower discount tier collapse.
- For packaging, explicit language that "token pools are monthly and do not carry over unless specified in the SOW" (we can mark the SOW if you want token carryover).

Attached is the pricing matrix (v3) and a short note with the proposed redline language for the flip clause. Want to avoid back-and-forth later with legal — if you can flag what procurement needs, I can get Marissa and Karthik to prepare the redline.

Next step: if this approach sounds acceptable, propose a 30-minute call this afternoon to lock wording.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake

Jordan —

Appreciate the proactive framing. High level response from procurement/legal: we do not agree to immediate retroactive loss of discount for a single short dip. Two asks from our side:

1) Grace period: We prefer 90 days (three billing cycles) before any downgrade is enacted. That gives us time to smooth traffic and apply credits where suitable.
2) Packaging: Novus uses monthly token pools but we have a small carryover allowance (up to 10% unused tokens) for pilot workloads. That needs to be captured in the SOW — we will attach an updated SOW with that clause.

I'll attach the SOW with our internal procurement annotations. We're open to the flip concept as a last-resort stabilizer, but need the smoothing and an ops-level rollback/cure.

Proposing a 30-minute sync at 15:00 PT if that works for you and your legal folks.

Best,
Emma Liu

Emma / team —

Thanks for the context, Emma. I took a pass at a customer-facing redline that preserves Redwood's ability to protect economic integrity while honoring Novus's operational realities. Key points below; redline doc attached (redline_flip_clause.docx).

Proposed redline summary:
- Smoothing window: 90-day cure period before discount tier reversion. The reversion, if triggered, is prospective to the first bill after the cure window concludes (no retroactive clawbacks).
- Warning and remediation: Redwood will send a notice after the first month below threshold; Novus will have 30 days to submit a remediation plan to avoid downgrade.
- Pilot carryover: Allow up to 10% carryover for named pilot workloads for the first 6 months post-go-live; any permanent carryover requires explicit SOW language.
- Packaging clarity: Define Pack A/B token definitions inline in Exhibit B to avoid ambiguity — e.g., "Pack A = 10M inference tokens/month, non-transferable except for pilot carryover as defined in SOW."

If Novus is comfortable with "prospective-only" reversion and a 90-day window, I think legal will be able to finalize without further substantive edits. If you prefer 60 days, we can take that as a concession but would like an operational notification and remediation requirement.

Jordan — if we do the 90/90 (90-day smoothing + 90-day pilot period) I suggest we capture that in the order form as short bullets and attach the redline to the DocuSign packet so procurement can see live language.

Marissa Cole

Emma / Jordan / Marissa —

Thanks — reading Marissa's redline now. Operationally, Novus's request for 90 days is reasonable given their burst profile. Proposed final compromise for tonight's sync:

- 90-day smoothing window (no retroactive adjustments).
- If two consecutive 90-day windows are below commit (i.e., sustained drop over ~180 days), pricing may be recalibrated prospectively.
- Pilot carryover of up to 10% for named workloads for first 6 months; thereafter carryover only by explicit SOW amendment.
- Add a short ops playbook clause: Redwood will provide a one-time consumption report and a remediation checklist within 10 business days of a Notice.

I'll be on the 15:00 PT call to present that compromise. Jordan — can you confirm who from Novus legal will join? Sara Bennett was cc'd earlier; if she can make the call that would be ideal.
